old: Most community projects begin in the wrong order: land first, vision in a document, ownership concentrated because somebody had the money, and emotional preparation deferred until everyone has more time.
new: One of the main problems I see with how people go about building community is that they do the steps in the wrong order. They get the land first, put the vision in a document, let ownership pile up with whoever had the money, and put off the emotional preparation until everyone has more time.
why: B's opening sentence; the published list of the wrong steps (both calls dropped it) as one run-on sentence

old: The better order is less cinematic. Practice together. Process a real conflict. Clarify values. Test membership. Decide ownership and exit. Then consider land.
new: The better order is less cinematic, more like this: practice together, process a real conflict, clarify your values, test membership, decide ownership and exit, and only then think about land.
why: B's "It's more like this:" and its one run-on list; Joel's order (2026-10-16 23:38) step by step, every step his (B had "figure out who you want in" for testing membership, and no real conflict), and the published "less cinematic"

old: The economic path should be staged the same way. A cluster of cooperating households can first take basic internal life out of purchase while outside earners contribute a defined share. It should move to a common purse only after it can provision members reliably and allocate the common fairly. Reducing or eliminating outside money should emerge from demonstrated capacity, not from declaring money impure while somebody else quietly pays the tax bill.
new: Likewise, the economic side has to go in stages. You're probably not going to be able to fly straight to the economic destination! Start with a cluster of households where nobody has to buy the basics of life inside the cluster anymore, and anyone making money on the outside contributes a set share. Only after you've proven that you can reliably provide for everybody, and fairly decide who gets what from the common, should you move to a common purse. Cutting back on outside money, or getting rid of it, comes from what you've shown you can do. ("Money is impure!" is a weird thing to say while somebody else is quietly paying the tax bill.)
why: A's sentences and its aside; the published staging "the same way", the common purse only after the group can provision members reliably and allocate the common fairly, and outside money reduced from demonstrated ability (A ran the two together)

Jobs, kids, pets, debt, a mortgage, a sick parent, or several of these arranged in a circle... That's fine! The most important pl/ork doesn't need land anyway.
